Using taxadb

Source: vignettes/taxadb.Rmd
taxadb.Rmd

taxastand matches names against a reference taxonomy that you supply, but does not come with any reference databases itself. The taxadb package fills that gap: it provides versioned snapshots of several standard taxonomic databases (ITIS, Catalog of Life, GBIF, NCBI and others) that you can query from R. This vignette shows how to take a table from taxadb and use it as a taxastand reference, using ITIS as the example.

Get the data

Install taxadb, then ask for a provider’s taxonomic data in the Darwin Core (dwc) schema. The first call downloads the snapshot (a Parquet file) to a local directory; later calls reuse it.

library(taxadb)
library(dplyr)
library(taxastand)

# Check which data versions are available to download
available_versions()
#> [1] "2026"  "22.12"

itis <- taxa_tbl(provider = "itis", schema = "dwc")
colnames(itis)
#>  [1] "taxonID"                  "scientificName"          
#>  [3] "taxonRank"                "acceptedNameUsageID"     
#>  [5] "taxonomicStatus"          "kingdom"                 
#>  [7] "phylum"                   "class"                   
#>  [9] "order"                    "family"                  
#> [11] "genus"                    "specificEpithet"         
#> [13] "infraspecificEpithet"     "vernacularName"          
#> [15] "scientificNameAuthorship" "update_date"

The columns taxastand uses are taxonID, acceptedNameUsageID, taxonomicStatus and scientificName. taxadb has all of them, with one catch: in taxadb the author is in a separate column, scientificNameAuthorship, but taxastand matches on the author and wants it as part of scientificName. ts_format_ref() takes care of this, and of the other steps needed to turn a table like this into a reference.

Make a reference

Whole databases are large (ITIS has about one million names), so for this vignette we will only use a single fern family:

ref <- itis |>
  filter(family == "Polypodiaceae") |>
  collect() |>
  ts_format_ref()

count(ref, taxonomicStatus)
#>   taxonomicStatus   n
#> 1        accepted 172
#> 2         synonym 137

ts_format_ref() pastes the author onto the name, drops rows above species rank (such as the genus Polypodium itself), and keeps the columns taxastand needs (plus taxonRank). If your table uses other column names, map them with the col_map argument. You can also record where the data came from with source, which is stored with the result. ts_format_ref() does not check the table for errors (for example, synonyms that point to a missing accepted name); the dwctaxon package can validate Darwin Core taxonomic data with dwctaxon::dct_validate().

The reference has accepted names and their synonyms, which is what resolving a name needs. It has 309 names. Synonyms look like this (acceptedNameUsageID points to the accepted name):

ref |>
  filter(taxonomicStatus == "synonym", lengths(strsplit(scientificName, " ")) > 2) |>
  head(5)
#>        taxonID acceptedNameUsageID taxonomicStatus               scientificName
#> 1 ITIS:1215188        ITIS:1215372         synonym Aglaomorpha meyeniana Schott
#> 2 ITIS:1215355        ITIS:1215353         synonym Polypodium chrysolepis Hook.
#> 3 ITIS:1215443        ITIS:1215226         synonym       Grammitis linearis Sw.
#> 4 ITIS:1215445        ITIS:1215204         synonym    Polypodium normale D. Don
#> 5 ITIS:1215450         ITIS:897672         synonym Acrostichum polypodioides L.
#>   taxonRank
#> 1   species
#> 2   species
#> 3   species
#> 4   species
#> 5   species

Resolve names

From here it is the usual taxastand workflow. For a large reference, prepare it once with ts_optimize_ref() (not really necessary here, but demonstrated for completeness).

ref_prepared <- ts_optimize_ref(ref)

queries <- c(
  "Polypodium vulgare L.",
  "Phymatodes scolopendria (Burm. f.) Ching",
  "Microsorum scolopendria",
  "Pleopeltis polylepis var. erythrolepis (Weath.) T. Wendt",
  "Polypodium pelucidum Kaulf."
)

res <- ts_resolve_names(queries, ref_prepared, match_no_auth = TRUE)
res[match(queries, res$query), c("query", "resolved_name", "matched_status", "match_type")]
#>                                                      query
#> 1                                    Polypodium vulgare L.
#> 5                 Phymatodes scolopendria (Burm. f.) Ching
#> 2                                  Microsorum scolopendria
#> 3 Pleopeltis polylepis var. erythrolepis (Weath.) T. Wendt
#> 4                              Polypodium pelucidum Kaulf.
#>                                              resolved_name matched_status
#> 1                                    Polypodium vulgare L.       accepted
#> 5                Microsorum scolopendria (Burm. f.) Copel.        synonym
#> 2                Microsorum scolopendria (Burm. f.) Copel.       accepted
#> 3 Pleopeltis polylepis var. erythrolepis (Weath.) T. Wendt       accepted
#> 4                             Polypodium pellucidum Kaulf.       accepted
#>    match_type
#> 1       exact
#> 5       exact
#> 2 auto_noauth
#> 3       exact
#> 4  auto_fuzzy

The rows are in the order of the queries. The first and fourth queries are accepted names that match exactly, and the fifth matches an accepted name after a spelling correction (auto_fuzzy). Phymatodes scolopendria (second) is an ITIS synonym, so it resolves to the accepted Microsorum scolopendria. The third query has no author, so it matched by ignoring the author (auto_noauth, which match_no_auth = TRUE allows).

Note that we did not need to remove the genus-level names ourselves: ts_format_ref() already did that. If you build a reference some other way and leave them in, the taxastand parser drops them and warns that they were excluded.

Other databases

The same steps work for other taxadb providers. Below, we list the providers that have the Darwin Core (dwc) schema, which is the one taxastand needs:

available_providers() |>
  filter(schema == "dwc")
#>   provider schema
#> 1      col    dwc
#> 2       fb    dwc
#> 3     gbif    dwc
#> 4     itis    dwc
#> 5     ncbi    dwc
#> 6      ott    dwc
#> 7      slb    dwc

To use a different provider, change provider in taxa_tbl() to one of these. Check colnames() before using, since the columns may differ between databases and may require different treatment to get them into a format that taxastand can use.

Some of the providers are described here:

Provider provider = Notes
Catalog of Life "col" Broad coverage, all kingdoms
GBIF backbone "gbif" Used by the GBIF occurrence database
ITIS "itis" Mostly North American taxa
NCBI "ncbi" Names of organisms in sequence databases
Open Tree of Life "ott" Names in the Open Tree of Life
FishBase "fb" Fishes
SeaLifeBase "slb" Marine organisms other than fishes

Check each provider’s license before reusing a table.

Reproducibility

taxadb snapshots are versioned. Pass version = to taxa_tbl() (see available_versions()) and record it with your results, so that the reference is the same the next time you run the analysis. Cite both the provider and taxadb.

The results in this vignette were made with ITIS snapshot 2026 and taxadb 0.3.0.
